notes: RBox contraction paired with technology-replace-0018: it removes the revision's original property (functionality of 'was first released in'), so every query expects 'does not know'; the propositional questions follow strong Kleene. The instances are the revision's (Sinclair QL 1984, BBC Micro 1981); the first asks whether the premise rules out a second first-release year (yes), the second whether the QL could also have been first released in 1986 (no), and the cross-lingual queries ask the second. Residual risk: 'first released' carries its uniqueness in the words themselves, so a model may keep it through the sense of 'first'; a 'no' is a kept property, never a sign the removal worked. Near unrelated asks the same property of a non-technology fact that stays as it was (contraction is exempt from Rule 7); far asks about an unrelated relation. hops counts the prompt's premise as one bridge.
